column1: # Shared test vectors. Both implementations must reproduce every row.
# Tab-separated. Lines starting with '#' are comments; blank lines are ignored.
# name       a label, for test output
# precision  -1 minute, 0 second, 1 millisecond (the CLI default is 0)
# clock_ms   the injected clock, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch UTC
# env        injected state and options, '-' for none (see below)
# The clock is always injected in milliseconds; coarser precisions truncate
# toward zero, and the truncation rows below pin that down.
# The env column is a comma-separated list of key=value pairs. Unset keys take
# the defaults shown, so a row only states what it cares about:
#   mac=02005E100000              %m, 48 bits of hex, no separators
#   rand=                         the random stream %g and %r draw from, hex
#   hashchars=8                   symbols kept from a hashed component
# Component rules, in full, because the vectors are the spec:
#   %d  the clock as the precision's unit count since the Unix epoch UTC
#   %h  %u  %f  SHA-256 of the raw name, hex uppercase, converted from base 16;
#       the rightmost hashchars symbols. With nohash=1 the name goes out
#   %m  the MAC as a 48-bit number, converted from base 16
#   %g  16 bytes drawn from the random stream with the UUID v4 version and
#       variant bits forced, converted from base 16 as a 128-bit number
#   %r  enough bytes drawn from the random stream to fill randchars symbols,
#       converted from base 16; the rightmost randchars symbols. One byte per
#       symbol covers any base up to 256 symbols; above that a symbol carries
#       more than eight bits, so the draw is ceil(randchars * bits / 8) instead
#       and the leading symbol still varies.
# %g and %r draw from the stream in the order they appear in the format.
# Output is zero-padded to a fixed width per component, chosen to hold that
# component's largest value: the horizon year 3000 for %d, 48 bits for %m, 128
# bits for %g. Hashed and random components are fixed at their configured
# symbol count. Padding uses each alphabet's zero digit, which for 32w is '2'
# Fixed width is what makes byte-order sort match chronological order, and it
# also lets a multi-component identifier be split by offset. Identifiers of
# different precisions have different widths and do not sort against each
# other - same caveat as mixing bases.
# Width is counted in symbols throughout, never in bytes. The wide bases at the
# end of this file, 64tt and up, have digits of two to four bytes each, so
# every padded and every truncated component there also pins down that the cut
# falls on a symbol boundary rather than mid-digit.
# Hashed components: SHA-256 of the name, converted from base 16, rightmost
# hash_chars is configurable. 43 is the full width of a SHA-256 in base 62,
# so that row also covers a hash that renders short and needs left-filling.
# Hashing off: the name goes out literally, unconverted and unpadded.
# MAC: 48 bits, so the width holds any address. The low row is the padding case.
# UUID v4: 16 bytes drawn from the random source, version and variant bits
# forced, then converted as a 128-bit number. The zero row shows those bits.
# Random: one byte drawn per requested symbol, rightmost random_chars kept.
# Composites: components render in format order, and %g then %r draw from the
# The wide bases. Same components, digits of two to four bytes each.
